actions: adduct toes 3-5 toward the axial line (digit 2)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: 3 separate small unipennate muscles (TA: interossei plantares I-III) -- the foot's structural analog of the hand's palmar interossei, again referenced to digit 2 rather than digit 3.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

trigger_points.location_description: Palpated on the plantar aspect between the metatarsal shafts of digits 3-5, deep in the forefoot.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Pain targets the digit each plantar interosseous serves -- the plantar (and to a lesser extent dorsal) surface of the associated toe and the plantar surface of its metatarsal.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Tight or narrow-toed footwear, prolonged standing/walking, and toe-gripping activities.
trigger_points.notes: Described together with the dorsal interossei by Travell & Simons as having analogous, digit-specific referral patterns; can mimic interdigital (Morton's) neuroma or MTP joint synovitis.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2 (Lower Extremities), 1999 -- as cited in secondary summaries (e.g. Morningside Acupuncture NYC 'Interossei of Foot Trigger Points', triggerpoints.net 'Interossei of Foot') describing the digit-specific plantar/dorsal referral pattern shared with the dorsal interossei
